title: Lane file
description: One lane of a project's plan record. The filename is the lane and the ranking domain computes order from entry facts.

lane.description: Must equal the file basename so a pasted fragment remains self-describing.

stories.description: The entries that belong to this lane. The ranking domain computes their order on every read.

allOf.description: A session claim belongs to a work lane and nowhere else. An entry in a planning lane has nobody acting on it, and a closed entry's locator would point at a session nobody will resume. The transition strips the claim on the way out, inside the same transaction as the lane change.

id.description: The title's slug, plus at most a qualifying postfix where that slug was taken. The id is the story document's filename stem. No consumer parses its interior.

needs_id.description: A dependency target: a bare id naming an entry in this record, or <alias>#<id> naming an entry in the peer that the plan configuration's peers section binds to that alias. The two forms mean the same thing, which is closed before this entry is eligible, and the graph, the eligibility rule, and the acyclicity proof treat them identically. The prefixed form is split exactly once, on the first separator: the alias half resolves in the peer table and the id half is carried whole, so the rule that no consumer parses an id survives. A prefixed id must be written double-quoted, which no schema can check because a schema reads a value the parser already unquoted; the canonical-subset parser holds that rule.

path.description: One relative path, resolved against the host's project root, exactly as an Amends path is. No leading or trailing separator, no empty segment, no dot segment, and no whitespace, so a one-line flow sequence stays unambiguous. The glob characters are excluded because a touch item is one exact path: exact paths give a deterministic overlap set, and a pattern language brings containment questions and false precision. Nothing resolves the path against a tree — the record cannot see the host's repository, and a prediction that had to exist already could never name new work.

session_ref.description: A session reference: one alias naming a table in the plan configuration's session_adapters section, one separator, and the opaque key that adapter's commands accept. The token is split exactly once, on the one separator, and the key half is carried whole because no consumer parses it. A prefixed reference must be written double-quoted, which no schema can check because a schema reads a value the parser already unquoted; the canonical-subset parser holds that rule. The cross-file checker resolves the alias against the declaration.

type.description: The kind of work and the condition for the worked-example gate.

points.description: Units of irreducible human judgment. Work above 3 must split.

delay_cost.description: When waiting harms this entry. Immediate sorts before absence, deferred sorts after absence, and absence is ordinary work without an added value.

needs.description: Ids that must be closed before this story is eligible. An id may carry an alias prefix and name an entry in an attached peer.

touches.description: The paths this entry's work probably changes, created, modified, or removed. Required on every landed entry, and an empty sequence is the decided form for work that changes no file: it says the author considered the question, where an absent key would say only that the entry is incomplete. Imprecise on purpose and checked against no tree. At most 12 items, which bounds the surface a reader compares rather than measuring complexity — points count judgments, and a story touching one central protocol file is often harder than one touching ten generated fixtures. Work predicting more paths splits along its outcomes. Every path a story's Amends section names appears here, which the cross-file checker decides because the assertion is in the document and the list is in this file. An overlap between two entries is advisory: it adds no edge, gates no transition, and enters no order computation.

session.description: The coding session acting on this entry, as one <alias>#<key> locator. Optional, and permitted in the work lanes alone: its absence honestly says the record makes no session claim, which is what covers work performed without a resolvable coding session, so nobody needs a synthetic adapter alias. The record stores the locator and nothing else — whether the session runs, where it listens, and what it is working on stay owned by the session system and are resolved on use. A claim is not a lock: it blocks nobody, expires against nothing, and gates no transition.

epic.description: Id of one epic document at <plan zone>/epics/<id>.md, where the zone is the directory this file lives two levels below. Ids are unique across stories and epics alike, so one id names one thing. Single-valued and never a sequencing fact.

tags.description: Free board labels. Nothing gates on a tag.

branch.description: The code branch carrying this entry's work — an explicit cross-reference, because plan and code no longer share commits. Opaque to every check beyond shape: the record cannot verify another repository.

outcome.description: Required in closed.yml and forbidden elsewhere.

closed.description: Required in closed.yml and forbidden elsewhere; used to derive velocity.

delivered.description: The commit that delivered the work, as its identifier in the host's version control. Meaningful in closed.yml only, like outcome and closed; the same standing as branch — stated, searchable, never verified.

succeeded_by.description: Required when outcome is reshaped and forbidden otherwise.

summary.description: One capped paragraph restating what this entry is, so a lane file answers without a file read per row. The story document stays the source of truth; this is a restatement of it and never a second specification. Double-quote it: an unquoted scalar carrying a colon is ambiguous under YAML. One line, no leading or trailing whitespace, because the record is parsed by a flat canonical subset.

note.description: Free prose about the entry's handling rather than about its subject — why it is parked, who is waiting on it, what a reader should know before picking it up. What the work is belongs in summary. Nothing parses it.
